i1-a.alt: Tangier long ago, seen from a hill at sunrise: white houses with flat roofs and a mosque tower climbing a hill above a blue bay, boats in the harbour. No people in front.

i1-b.alt: Ibn Battuta stands on a hill above Tangier at dawn, looking east into the far distance, the sea shining behind him, wind in his cloak.
i1-b.scene: a young Moroccan man of about twenty-one with warm light-brown skin, a short neat dark beard and kind, curious eyes, in a cream hooded wool travelling cloak over a long white tunic, a white turban and a leather bag across his chest stands on a hill above Tangier at dawn, looking east into the far distance, the sea shining behind him, wind in his cloak.

i1-d.alt: Ibn Battuta walks along a dusty road beside the sea, away from the town, while small birds fly up from a nest in a tree beside the road.

i3-c.alt: Kind Syrian men gather round the boy in the lane, one pointing helpfully down the street, as the boy gathers the broken blue-and-white pieces into his hands.

i4-d.alt: At dawn Ibn Battuta stands on a hill outside Makkah with his bag on his shoulder, looking out over many roads leading away in different directions.
